title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 125
paragraphs: Now the family of the Alcmaeonidae had already been prominent at Athens from the earliest times, and they became very greatly distinguished from the time of Alcmaeon and of Megacles after him. For Alcmaeon son of Megacles made himself of use to the Lydians sent from Croesus at Sardis to the oracle at Delphi, and assisted them energetically. When Croesus heard from the Lydians who had gone to the oracle that this man had served him well, he summoned him to Sardis, and when he arrived Croesus offered him as a gift as much gold as he could carry away on his own person at one time. With such a gift in view, Alcmaeon made preparations and resorted to these devices. He put on a large tunic, letting a deep fold of it hang open at the front, and he pulled on the widest boots he could find. So equipped he went into the treasury to which they led him. There he threw himself onto a heap of gold dust, and first he packed along the sides of his legs as much gold as his boots would hold; then he filled the whole fold of his tunic with gold and sprinkled some of the gold dust on his hair and took some into his mouth. Having done this, he came out of the treasury, dragging his boots with difficulty and looking like anything on earth except a man — for his mouth was stuffed full and every part of him was bulging. Croesus burst out laughing when he saw him, and not only gave him everything he was carrying but presented him with even more besides, of no less value. So this family became enormously wealthy, and this same Alcmaeon of whom I speak became a breeder of chariot horses and won a victory at Olympia.
